content: 1. The concurrent use of sodium oxybate with alcohol or insomnia medications is contraindicated due to the risk of additive central nervous system (CNS) depression. 2. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of canagliflozin by increasing its metabolism. Close monitoring is advised, and alternative antihyperglycemic agents should be considered in patients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 73 mL/min/1.73 m². 3. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 4. Cannabidiol increases the levels or effects of phenobarbital by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Dose reductions of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates may be necessary when co-administered with cannabidiol. 5. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of capivasertib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of alternative drugs is recommended, as strong or moderate CYP3A inducers can decrease capivasertib exposure and reduce its efficacy. 6. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of capmatinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 7. Phenobarbital and captopril may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to a greater reduction in blood pressure. Blood pressure should be closely monitored. 8. Carbachol increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction effect is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are necessary. 9. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of carbamazepine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 10. Phenobarbital and carbinoxamine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 11. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cariprazine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated, as CYP3A4 is essential for the formation and elimination of cariprazine's active metabolites. 12. Phenobarbital and cariprazine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Phenobarbital and carisoprodol both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 14. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of carvedilol by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. A higher beta-blocker dose may be required during co-administration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. 15. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of celecoxib by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 16. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of celiprolol by increasing its metabolism. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. Close monitoring is advised. 17. Phenobarbital and cenobamate both increase sedation. Cenobamate increases phenobarbital levels or effects through an unspecified mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 18. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ceritinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 19. Cevimeline increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction effect is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are necessary. 20. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cevimeline by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 21. Phenobarbital and chloral hydrate both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 22. Chloramphenicol increases phenobarbital levels by decreasing its metabolism, while phenobarbital reduces chloramphenicol levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 23. Phenobarbital and chlordiazepoxide both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 24. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of chloroquine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 25. Phenobarbital and chlorpheniramine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 26. Phenobarbital and chlorpromazine both increase sedation. Chlorpromazine enhances the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergism, while belladonna alkaloids reduce chlorpromazine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Close monitoring is advised. 27. Phenobarbital and chlorzoxazone both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 28. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cilostazol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 29. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cimetidine by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 30. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cinacalcet by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 31. Phenobarbital and cinnarizine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 32. Belladonna alkaloids and cisatracurium both decrease cholinergic effects. Phenobarbital reduces the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 33. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of citalopram by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is necessary. 34. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing its elimination. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 35. Phenobarbital and clemastine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 36. Phenobarbital and clobazam both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 37. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of clomipramine by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids and clomipramine both decrease cholinergic effects. Barbiturates may increase adverse effects, including respiratory depression, with toxic doses of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs). With therapeutic doses of TCAs, barbiturates increase metabolism and decrease blood concentrations of TCAs. Close monitoring is required. 38. Phenobarbital and clonazepam both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of clonazepam by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 39. Phenobarbital and clonidine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 40. Phenobarbital increases the levels or effects of clopidogrel by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inducers may enhance the metabolism of clopidogrel to its active metabolite. Patients should be monitored for increased antiplatelet effects when CYP3A4 inducers are used with clopidogrel. 41. Phenobarbital and clorazepate both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of clorazepate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 42. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of clotrimazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 43. Phenobarbital and clozapine both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of clozapine by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Belladonna alkaloids reduce clozapine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Clozapine enhances the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergism. Close monitoring is necessary. 44. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for loss of virologic response from cobicistat. 45. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cobimetinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration, as strong or moderate CYP3A inducers can decrease cobimetinib systemic exposure by more than 80%, reducing its efficacy. 46. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of topical cocaine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 47. Phenobarbital and codeine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 48. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of colchicine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 49. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of conivaptan by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is necessary. 50. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Close monitoring is recommended. 51. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of vaginal conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Close monitoring is necessary. 52. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of copanlisib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 53. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cortisone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Close monitoring is required. 54. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of crizotinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid the concomitant use of strong CYP3A inducers. 55. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of cyanocobalamin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 56. Belladonna alkaloids and cyclizine both decrease cholinergic effects. Cyclizine and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 57. Phenobarbital and cyclobenzaprine both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids and cyclobenzaprine both decrease cholinergic effects. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 58. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 59. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of cyclosporine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Close monitoring is necessary. 60. Phenobarbital and cyproheptadine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 61. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of dabigatran by influencing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 62. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of dabrafenib by increasing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 63. Phenobarbital reduces the effects of dalteparin by increasing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 64. Phenobarbital and dantrolene both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of dantrolene by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 65. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of daprodustat through other mechanisms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. CYP2C8 inducers may decrease daprodustat exposure, potentially reducing its efficacy. Hemoglobin levels should be monitored, and daprodustat doses adjusted when initiating or discontinuing CYP2C8 inducers. 66. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of dapsone by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 67. Phenobarbital increases the toxicity of topical dapsone by altering its metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary, as it may induce methemoglobinemia. 68. Phenobarbital and daridorexant both increase sedation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of daridorexant by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 69. Belladonna alkaloids and darifenacin both decrease cholinergic effects. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of darifenacin by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required.
